newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares trade firmer as panic subsides.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares trade firmer as panic subsides.

text.p: Greek shares were trading 0.98 percent higher after opening sharply lower and brokers said the fall in the last three days was unjustified and the market would consolidate on Tuesday.

"On Monday the index fell by an all-time record 7.45 percent. At these cheap prices, investors were attracted back into the market and slowly started buying again," said Nikos Stylianou, a broker at Capital Securities.
The market could consolidate around 1,200 points on Tuesday and then start rising again, he added.
Another analyst said the bourse's fall was an exaggerated negative reaction to its strong rise.

"The selling panic will subside on Tuesday as buyers will gradually emerge. The fall of the past three days was an overreaction to the bourse's previous abrupt rise," said Iakovos Diamantopoulos, a broker at Hermes Brokerage.
He expected the market to be nervous and volatile with large fluctuations in the next few days, before stabilising.
"However, the market will manage to consolidate within the week. It will then start rising again, as there are strong and solid reasons whereas the fall was only a result of panic," he said.
Another analyst said that a calmer day at the bourse was expected.
"The index cannot continue to fall. Investors will be reasonable and start buying at these levels, instead of selling in panic" said Panagiotis Kontalexis, a broker at Egnatia Securities.
The Athens general share index was trading 0.98 percent or 11.82 points higher at 1218.36 points from Monday's 1206.54, after opening at 1200.15.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 943.00-981.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, were trading 250 drachmas higher at 5,650.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $30.66-$32.31. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 1,258-1,426 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 9,562-10,065 drachmas.
